s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative infection of a medical device implant site with signs of local inflammation and possible systemic infection
salient_findings: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
Elevated inflammatory syndrome on laboratory studies
Presence of Staphylococcus epidermidis on swab of the lesion
key_facts: 72-year-old man with no prior medical history
Underwent dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
Procedure was for 2:1 atrioventricular block
Procedure was uneventful
Discharged the next day
Presented with fever on postoperative day 4
Fever was 38.1°C
Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
Elevated inflammatory syndrome on laboratory studies
Blood cultures were obtained
Antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
Lesion darkened and enlarged by day 7 despite antibiotic therapy
Blood cultures remained negative by day 7

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, which is consistent with a pocket infection

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal biofilm infection
shortlist.why_kept: Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, which is a common cause of biofilm infections

shortlist.label: Surgical site infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed signs of infection, including fever and an inflamed lesion, at the surgical site

shortlist.label: Device-related endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Although blood cultures were negative, the patient has a prosthetic device and developed signs of infection, making endocarditis a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Prosthetic device infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a prosthetic device and developed signs of infection, including fever and an inflamed lesion, which is consistent with a device infection

raw.rationale: The patient presented with an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the pacemaker implant site on postoperative day 4, which is consistent with a pacemaker pocket infection. The presence of Staphylococcus epidermidis on the swab of the lesion and the failure of the lesion to improve with antibiotic therapy further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal biofilm infection
rejected.why: While Staphylococcus epidermidis was isolated, the primary issue is the infection of the pacemaker pocket, not just the biofilm aspect.

rejected.label: Surgical site infection
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes pacemaker pocket infection, but the specific details point more directly to a pacemaker pocket infection.

rejected.label: Device-related endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of valve involvement or other signs of endocarditis, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Prosthetic device infection
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes pacemaker pocket infection, but the specific details provided make pacemaker pocket infection the more precise diagnosis.
